title: Autonomous DDIL edge PED node with sensor-to-map exploitation (georegistered drone video, minute-scale 3D and change overlays without reach-back) and resilient reconciliation to AIDP/Maven
problem: Brigade-and-below intelligence nodes and small-unit drone operators cannot exploit organic sensor data locally for 72+ hours while disconnected (detect, georegister, build 3D/change overlays on the TAK map) and then reconcile those products conflict-free with AIDP/Maven Smart System when links return, so today they either wait for reach-back or hand-plot and re-enter data.
echelons: division/MDTF intelligence nodes (TITAN Basic, AIDP edge kits)

user.exact_role: Brigade/battalion S2 intelligence analyst (35F) and brigade geospatial engineer (12Y), plus company-level sUAS operators and company intelligence support teams who own the drone video; SOF team intelligence NCOs as a second user class
user.echelon: Battalion and brigade (primary); company (sensor-to-map half); division/MDTF (AIDP/TITAN Basic edge node half)
organization_examples: XVIII Airborne Corps units running Scarlet Dragon (82nd, 101st Airborne)
Transformation-in-Contact brigades at NTC/JRTC rotations (e.g., NTC 26-02 per MIPB)
Multi-Domain Task Forces (3rd MDTF, Talisman Sabre 25)
USSOCOM PEO SOF Warrior elements (Farsight users)
Theater Army ACE nodes using AIDP as the common intelligence picture

current_workflow: Organic sensors (sUAS such as Skydio X10D, ground sensors, radios) record locally; CoT position/telemetry streams to ATAK on the local multicast network.

When a link exists, raw FMV/imagery is pushed up to brigade/division AIDP edge kit, TITAN, or enterprise AIDP cloud / Maven Smart System; enterprise models and analysts detect, annotate and build products.

Products (overlays, 3D, change reports) come back down hours to days later over the same congested link; at company level 3D/2D products are often built on the drone or ground station (Skydio Onboard Modeling, Reveal Farsight) and shared by screenshot, voice or file.

When disconnected, analysts screen video manually, hand-plot on ATAK or PowerPoint, and 'swivel chair' data between NIPR/SIPR and between intel, C2 and fires systems (MIPB 'Swivel Chair War', NTC 26-02).
When links return, locally produced data is re-uploaded or re-entered by hand; there is no documented conflict-free reconciliation of the local store with AIDP/MSS.
current_solution: AIDP (Palantir) enterprise cloud with limited edge kits; TITAN Advanced/Basic ground stations (Palantir prime, Anduril hardware) at division/corps; Maven Smart System at theater/joint; TurbineOne Frontline Perception System for edge object recognition (Army IDIQ Sept 2025, JIOP April 2026); Reveal Farsight for offline drone 3D (STRATFI, SOCOM use); Edgybees Argus for FMV georegistration (USAF multi-award); Skydio X10D onboard 3D modeling and offline ATAK streaming; Vantor OWT 3D Tiles in ATAK and Luno B change detection at enterprise; manual screening and hand-plotting as the universal fallback.
failure: Two seams fail: (1) between the local edge store and the enterprise (AIDP/MSS) there is no fielded, vendor-neutral store-and-forward reconciliation for 72-hour disconnection - the AIDP Call for Solutions (July 2026) writes this as a new requirement rather than citing an existing capability; (2) between heterogeneous drone feeds and the TAK map there is no standard MISB-KLV-driven pipeline that yields georegistered overlays, incremental 3D and change alerts against a baseline in minutes offline - current products are tied to a specific drone (Skydio), a specific vendor workflow (Reveal), or need GPU/cloud (Vantor/Luno).

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: The problem is being solved piecewise by better-funded, earlier-arriving firms: TurbineOne (edge inference, $98.9M-ceiling Army IDIQ), Reveal (edge 3D, $33.6M STRATFI, SOCOM use since 2021), Edgybees (georegistration), Skydio (on-drone 3D, offline ATAK) and Palantir (AIDP edge kits, TITAN, MSS). What remains unsolved is the glue - drone-agnostic MISB/KLV-to-TAK pipeline, edge change detection against OWT/commercial baselines, and conflict-free reconciliation with AIDP/MSS - and that glue is unattractive to each incumbent because (a) the reconciliation target (AIDP/MSS data model and APIs) is controlled by the AIDP-Next winner and Open DAGIR onboarding, (b) integration work across dozens of formats (MISB, STANAG 4609/4676, CoT, NITF) earns little venture credit, (c) validating against military FMV requires being inside a program, and (d) buyers are split across PM IS&A (AIDP/TITAN), PEO Soldier/PM UAS (drones), PEO STRI (OWT), CDAO (MSS) and SOCOM, so no single office owns 'company drone to brigade intel to enterprise' end-to-end.
technical_wedge: Not the whole node (already occupied). The defensible slice is a vendor-neutral 'edge intel sync and sensor-to-map' middleware: (1) a local conflict-free store (CRDT/log-based) for detections, tracks, chips, overlays and 3D tiles with prioritized, bandwidth-aware store-and-forward and provable reconciliation against a mock AIDP/MSS/STAC endpoint after 72h; (2) a drone-agnostic ingest that takes any MISB 0601 KLV feed (Skydio, Teal, Parrot, Group 2/3 UAS) and produces georegistered footprints, incremental orthos/3D Tiles and change alerts versus an OWT/Cesium baseline on Jetson-class hardware, published to ATAK/TAK Server via standard CoT and data packages. Ship as a TAK plugin plus a headless edge service, with an adapter layer that the AIDP-Next prime or TITAN ecosystem partners can onboard.

mvp.what: Laptop/Jetson Orin edge box running: KLV-driven georegistration of commercial drone video, incremental 3D Tiles and change-vs-baseline overlays into ATAK-CIV within minutes offline; a local CRDT store of detections/overlays; simulated 72-hour disconnection with bandwidth capped at ~5% then reconciliation into a mock enterprise (PostGIS/STAC) with zero duplicate or lost records.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for the unclassified pipeline on commercial drones and open terrain: georegistration accuracy benchmarked against RTK ground truth, time-to-overlay, and a scripted DDIL reconciliation test; not yet integration with AIDP/MSS (requires program access).
mvp.what_it_must_prove: (a) Georegistration error and time-to-overlay on unmodified commercial drones without cloud; (b) change alerts against an OWT-like baseline with acceptable false-alarm rate; (c) 72-hour disconnected operation with deterministic reconciliation and provenance; (d) that an S2 or drone operator adopts it in a soldier touchpoint without a field service engineer.

data_requirement.what: MISB-tagged drone video with accurate metadata across several airframes; baseline terrain/imagery (3D Tiles, orthos); labeled detections for the edge models (or reuse third-party models); for a credible demo, military FMV samples and the AIDP/MSS data model and API specifications.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Commercial drone video and open terrain are freely obtainable; MISB sample streams exist publicly; military FMV, AIDP/MSS schemas and TITAN interfaces are obtainable only inside an SBIR Phase II/OTA, CRADA, or as an onboarded ecosystem partner, and may carry export-control markings that constrain a non-U.S.-person founder's access (needs counsel).

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires a U.S. small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (armysbir.army.mil eligibility page); with one founder not assumed to be a U.S. person, the cap table must be structured so U.S.-person ownership/control exceeds 50% at award time (needs SBIR counsel). DIU CSOs and OTAs do not carry the SBIR ownership test but may apply FOCI-style review; any classified follow-on (SIPR data, TITAN integration) requires a facility clearance, where foreign ownership/control/influence mitigation and personnel clearances are assessed by DCSA - the non-U.S.-person founder would likely be excluded from classified work and from certain export-controlled technical data absent licenses. These are constraints to scope with counsel, not legal conclusions.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, and the AIDP-Next CfS effectively obliges the winner to. Palantir already ships AIDP edge kits and TITAN Basic; Anduril has Lattice Mesh and Klas compute; both can bundle an edge PED node and treat sync as internal plumbing. L3Harris (TITAN sub, DCGS lineage) can do the same via the HYDRA API. The sensor-to-map half is being absorbed by drone OEMs (Skydio) and STRATFI-funded Reveal.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Largely reject as a standalone company thesis. A startup wins only in the narrow, unglamorous seam: a vendor-neutral, standards-based (CoT/KLV/3D Tiles/STAC) reconciliation and sensor-to-map layer that works with any drone and any enterprise, which incumbents have little incentive to make vendor-neutral. That is a subcontract/onboarded-component business (TAK plugin, AIDP-Next team member, TITAN ecosystem partner), not a prime; it can be a good acqui-hire or feature business but not obviously a venture-scale one.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The unclassified MVP (commercial drones, ATAK-CIV, open terrain) carries low burden. Moving to military FMV, AIDP/MSS/TITAN integration and SIPR hosting raises burden to high: software specially designed for military ISR exploitation may fall under USML Category XI or EAR 600-series controls (classification requires counsel), an IL5 or SIPR ATO is needed, cleared staff and a facility clearance are needed for classified integration, and TAK plugin distribution to military users goes through TAK Product Center review.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: SBIR/STTR eligibility requires >50% U.S.-citizen/permanent-resident ownership and control; a non-U.S.-person founder may be unable to access ITAR-controlled technical data or military FMV without a license or exemption, cannot hold a U.S. security clearance, and could trigger FOCI mitigation for a facility clearance. Structuring options (ownership percentages, role limits, proxy/mitigation agreements, timing relative to a green card) must be reviewed with export-control and DCSA counsel before approaching Army customers; this card makes no legal determination.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Drone-agnostic georegistration, incremental 3D and change detection with offline sync have commercial analogues in public safety (wildfire, SAR, disaster response using ATAK-CIV/TAK), infrastructure inspection and mining, and allied civil protection; however commercial buyers already have Skydio/DJI/DroneDeploy/Pix4D cloud workflows, so the DDIL/reconciliation feature is only strongly valued by defense, public-safety and remote-industrial users.

defensibility.explanation: Algorithms (splatting, CRDTs, change detection) are largely open; defensibility would come from validated adapters to AIDP/MSS/TITAN/HYDRA, a TAK-certified plugin footprint on fielded devices, an IL5/SIPR accreditation, and soldier-validated workflow. Each of these is also exactly what the AIDP-Next prime can reproduce or gate, so defensibility is weak unless the government designates the sync layer as a government-owned or open interface the startup implements first.

why_now: In the last three years: AIDP rolled out globally (Oct 2024) and the Army wrote a 72-hour DDIL edge and MSS-exchange requirement into the AIDP-Next CfS (July 2026); TITAN entered production with a lighter Basic variant (Sept 2026); MSS became the mandated joint layer (>100K users, aggressive transition timeline, April-Sept 2026); Open DAGIR opened an onboarding path (2024); the Army standardized on Skydio X10D at company level (2025-2026) with MISB/CoT outputs; Jetson Orin-class edge compute and neural reconstruction (Gaussian splatting, 2023+) made minute-scale 3D on portable hardware feasible; NTC 26-02 and Iran/Ukraine operations documented that disconnected units fall back to manual workarounds.
killer_risk: Both halves of the gap already have funded occupants, and the seam between them is owned by the AIDP-Next winner: TurbineOne holds a $98.9M-ceiling Army IDIQ for edge object recognition, Reveal holds a $33.6M STRATFI and SOCOM use for edge 3D, Skydio ships on-drone 3D and offline ATAK streaming, and Palantir/Anduril will deliver the 72-hour DDIL edge node and MSS sync as part of AIDP-Next/TITAN. A two-founder team with a non-U.S.-person co-founder cannot get military FMV, AIDP/HYDRA interface specs or SIPR access fast enough to beat them, so the most likely outcome is a subcontract-sized feature business or an acqui-hire, not a company.

allied_extension: Somewhat more compelling with allies, but not enough to change the verdict. NATO bought MSS NATO sole-source (2025) and allied land forces (UK Digital Targeting Web, Germany D-LBO/TaWAN, Ukraine Delta/Kropyva) face the same disconnected-edge problem with fewer entrenched U.S. incumbents at the edge; Reveal already claims UK and Ukraine users and Quantum Systems/Helsing/ARX occupy German drone-to-C2 ground. A TAK/CoT-standard, drone-agnostic sensor-to-map layer is exportable to allies who use ATAK (UK, NATO SOF) and the German founder could pursue Bundeswehr/DIANA routes, but export licensing of a U.S.-developed ISR exploitation product and the non-U.S.-person founder's role would need counsel; allied sales are a later-stage add-on, not a reason to start.
